deviations: Engine sample: engine_data.dta taken as the paper's fighter/bomber engine file (it carries airframe-matched counts); US rows with non-missing ln_hp_per_lbs used without further filtering (85 engines). The paper text does not spell out how the file was built.

Spline: continuous two-piece linear spline in Stata mkspline form, before = min(year,1926), after = max(year-1926,0), so 1926 belongs to the before segment and the coefficients are segment slopes, not slope changes.
Equation (5) parameterized as a constant, a US indicator, a baseline spline on all observations (the UK/comparison slope) and spline x US (US slope minus UK slope).
notes: Data: airframe_data.dta (types fighter and bomber, US and UK, years 1918-1935, all years in the file) and engine_data.dta. OLS with lm(); HC1 robust SEs printed but no point estimates depend on them. Table 1 columns 1-2: US only, log wing load / log max speed on the spline plus a constant (N=116 wing load, 174 max speed). Columns 3-4: pooled US+UK (N=165, 233). Table 4 column 1: US engines, log hp per lb on the spline plus a liquid-cooled indicator plus a constant (N=85). Attempt-1 was exploratory (variable inspection, no RESULT lines). Attempt-2 printed RESULT lines, but its pooled regressions used separate US-only and UK-only splines, so the 'vs UK' coefficients were plain US slopes (identical to columns 1-2) instead of relative slopes. Found by self-review of the specification, not by comparison with any paper value; reparameterized for the final run (see attempt-2/feedback.txt). Kind is '' because neither 'error' nor 'claim' applies. Disclosure: while reading paper.txt for the method (the Table 1 notes area, lines 1055-1075), a garbled fragment of three bare numbers from the Table 1 extraction showed on screen; it was not searched for and the specification was not adjusted toward it. No .do/.R or result files (.tex/.log/.pdf) in the mount were opened.
